traits: White to pale grey cap, matt, as if frosted, 3 to 13 cm, dished in the centre with age; margin rolled and wavy
Decurrent gills, white then pink when ripe
Short stem, 2 to 5 cm, often off-centre and flared at the top
Soft white flesh with a strong smell of fresh flour that disappears when cooked
Grass and woodland edges, under broadleaves or conifers · summer to autumn, a few weeks before porcini
safetyNote: Toxic white clitocybes (muscarine) are sometimes mistaken for it: their gills stay white or cream and their spores are white, whereas its spores are pink. The floury smell is not enough: the livid pinkgill has it too.
